Nissan Celebrates 75 Years of Patrol, Signals Nameplate's Return to the US With Armada Patrol PRO-4X
38 photos
Photo: Nissan
The Japanese automaker Nissan has decided to mark the occasion of Patrol's 75th anniversary in America, too, although the iconic moniker hasn't been seen there since 1969, almost six decades ago.
Of course, the legendary Nissan Patrol has been alive and well in other regions – the Japanese automaker instead chose to use the Armada moniker starting in 2003. Initially, the first-generation Armada was made in Canton, Mississippi, based on the Nissan Titan pickup truck, but since 2016 the Armada moved to a new production location in Kanda, Kyushu, Japan, and started sharing the platform with the global Nissan Patrol.
The luxury version of both is dubbed the Infiniti QX80 (originally QX56), by the way. Now, Nissan has decided to reintroduce the iconic Patrol nameplate to the United States for the first time since 1969, “bringing one of the brand's most enduring and globally recognized badges back to American roads.” As such, for the 2027 model year, Armada's off-road-focused grade has been renamed Patrol PRO-4X instead of simply PRO-4X.
Nissan is taking advantage of Patrol’s 75th anniversary and marking the occasion in the United States, too, with the 2027 Armada Patrol PRO-4X, which enters production in November 2026, “further strengthens that bond, making the connection between Armada and Patrol closer than at any point in the model's history.” The Nissan Patrol first arrived in the US in 1962 through Datsun dealers, and it was initially among the few Nissan-badged vehicles sold in the US market until the early 1980s.
It was no longer offered after 1969 but “remained a popular choice in other markets, particularly the Middle East, where it has become known for its ability to conquer towering dunes.” Nissan explains a quirk: borrowed from the GT‑R, where it was used to keep the power up during tight corners, the Patrol has a special "scavenger" oil pump that enhances lubrication in driving conditions with “high g-forces,” allowing the SUV to climb even the steepest dunes.
Back to the 2027 Armada Patrol PRO-4X, it will become available soon as production of the renamed grade kicks off this month, and it comes with expanded looks and capability: fresh Nismo rock sliders and a Nismo roof rack, plus optional Nismo Axis wheels mated to BF Goodrich all-terrain tires.
"Patrol has defined adventure for 75 years, earning its reputation on some of the toughest terrain in the world. Bringing the Nissan Patrol name back to America through Armada is a natural fit, with both vehicles sharing the same iconic and proven platform," said Tiago Castro, senior vice president, U.S. Marketing & Sales, Nissan and INFINITI. "Armada Patrol PRO‑4X honors that legendary heritage while carrying its capability and confidence into Nissan's future."
The first outing of the 2027 Nissan Armada Patrol PRO-4X will be at the upcoming 2026 LA Auto Show (November 20-29). The grade has an electronic locking rear differential, Adaptive Electronic Air Suspension, eight selectable drive modes, a metal underbody skid plate, and advanced camera systems like Invisible Hood View, among others.
There’s also pricing information: the 2027 Nissan Armada SL 4x2 starts at $64,290 without destination and handling, which is an additional $2,275. The 4x4 version kicks off at $67,290, and the Armada Platinum 4x4 at $75,790. The renamed Armada Patrol PRO-4X is at least $78,990, while the Nismo and Platinum Reserve 4x4 tower above them at $80,690 and $84,590, respectively.
